findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before dispatching test.yml on main, also check for `queued` workflow_dispatch runs (not just `in_progress`), because the shared concurrency group with cancel-in-progress cancels them too.
evidence: Plan: "dispatch `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main`, first checking `gh run list --workflow test.yml --status in_progress` and waiting for any in-progress run"
.github/workflows/test.yml:36-40: `concurrency: group: test-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}` / `cancel-in-progress: true`

Evidence class: Partially-verified. gh run list's --status filter is used by the plan; the queued-vs-in_progress distinction is an inference from GitHub's run states, and I did not check it against --help here.
findings.finding: The pre-dispatch check waits only for runs with `--status in_progress`. test.yml's concurrency group is `test-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a new workflow_dispatch on main also cancels a dispatch run that is still `queued`. The check misses that case, and could cancel someone else's queued health run; the same concurrency rule could likewise cancel the plan's own measuring run before its Windows job finishes.
findings.location: Approach, step 1 (Measure): `gh run list --workflow test.yml --status in_progress`
scenarios: Another operator's health dispatch on main is queued (not yet in_progress) when step 1 dispatches. The new run cancels it, and the check did not see it.
A second dispatch on main while the measuring run is still active cancels it, so no Windows spans are recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: Check both states, e.g. `gh run list --workflow test.yml --event workflow_dispatch --branch main --status queued` and `... --status in_progress`, and wait for both lists to be empty before `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main`. Or read the spans from the next scheduled run (its concurrency group is different) instead of dispatching.

Absence: no Testing line or AC asserts that, after the switch, the main test still observes a maintenance/repack process outside the commit.
findings.finding: The plan validates the minimal crossing only through the sibling detector test. That control proves one thing: with the suppression absent, maintenance starts inside a commit. The main test is named `test_write_survives_foreground_maintenance_repack`, and its value also depends on rebar's explicit post-commit maintenance step actually running a repack. Under the old fill that repack was described as a repack of 20,000 objects. Two loose objects plus `gc.auto=1`/`maintenance.geometric-repack.auto=1` might not drive that explicit step to repack. This is likely if the explicit step runs under the same `_without_implicit_maintenance` env that appends `gc.auto=0`.
